scope: Append 14 source-linked selections to the remaining 12 shortlisted guides. Preserve all existing text, typography, illustrations, facts and practical pages. No canonical changes or main-book assembly.

oldVarieties.name: Bonica
oldVarieties.text: An early hybrid with large, dark-purple fruits. A practical choice for a warm greenhouse or polytunnel.

oldVarieties.name: Clara F1

oldVarieties.text: A traditional selection with long purple fruits. Keep as a heritage option for gardeners with a warm growing space.

oldVarieties.name: Bright Lights
oldVarieties.text: A colourful chard selection with stems in several shades. Harvest young leaves for salads or larger leaves and stems for cooking.

oldVarieties.name: Rhubarb Chard
oldVarieties.text: Red stalks and dark leaves make this chard decorative as well as useful. Treat it as a red-stemmed type unless a cultivar is specified.

oldVarieties.name: Spinach Beet
oldVarieties.text: A leaf beet grown for repeated picking of green leaves. Useful as a cooking green through a longer season than true spinach.

oldVarieties.name: Fordhook Giant
oldVarieties.text: A white-stemmed chard with broad green leaves. A useful kitchen choice when leaf yield matters more than mixed stem colours.

additions.name: Lucullus
additions.text: Pale stems and crinkled green leaves. Pick the outer leaves regularly for a continuing crop.

sourceValue.text: Also known as seakale beet or silver chard. It produces deep narrow roots rather than a swollen beetroot and is grown for broad leaves and thick edible midribs. White-stemmed types such as Lucullus, Fordhook Giant and White-Silver 2 are sometimes listed.

additions.name: White Silver 2
additions.text: Broad green leaves and white, fleshy stalks. Useful for both leafy greens and cooked stems.

oldVarieties.name: Boltardy
oldVarieties.text: A familiar round red beetroot valued for resistance to bolting. A useful choice for earlier sowings under suitable conditions.

oldVarieties.name: Pablo F1
oldVarieties.text: A round red beetroot producing uniform roots with good kitchen quality. Harvest young for tender roots.

oldVarieties.name: Cylindra
oldVarieties.text: Long, cylindrical red roots make even slices easy. Useful for cooking and pickling when shape matters more than round presentation.

oldVarieties.name: Chioggia
oldVarieties.text: A heritage beetroot with pink-and-white rings when cut raw. Grow for visual variety alongside a standard red beetroot.

oldVarieties.name: Forono
oldVarieties.text: An elongated red beetroot with a tidy shape for slicing. Retain as an established alternative to round-rooted selections.
